candidates.description: Cimetidine treatment inhibits tumor growth in A549 lung adenocarcinoma xenografts
candidates.citation_sentence: As described in the Registered Report (Kandela et al., 2015), we attempted a replication of the experiments reported in Figures 4C–D and Supplemental Figure 1 of Sirota et al., 2011.
candidates.notes: The effect is in the expected direction (cimetidine decreased tumor volume vs vehicle) but is not statistically significant at the Bonferroni-corrected threshold (uncorrected p=0.035, Bonferroni corrected p=0.105). Authors use hedging language ('While not statistically significant') and describe it as 'in the same direction as the original study.' [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Discovery and preclinical validation of drug indications using compendia of public gene expression data
candidates.description: Cimetidine treatment does not affect tumor growth in ACHN renal cell carcinoma xenografts
candidates.citation_sentence: As described in the Registered Report (Kandela et al., 2015), we attempted a replication of the experiments reported in Figures 4C–D and Supplemental Figure 1 of Sirota et al., 2011.
candidates.notes: Both the original study and this replication found no significant effect of cimetidine on ACHN tumors (original: no effect reported; replication: t(53)=-0.58, p=0.562). Authors say 'similar to the original study,' confirming the original null finding. However, the codebook's success criteria require a statistically significant effect in the same direction, which is absent here since neither the original nor replication had a significant effect. A second coder might plausibly code this as 'success' (confirming the original null) or 'failure' (no significant effect found). [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Discovery and preclinical validation of drug indications using compendia of public gene expression data
candidates.description: Doxorubicin treatment inhibits tumor growth in A549 lung adenocarcinoma xenografts
candidates.citation_sentence: As described in the Registered Report (Kandela et al., 2015), we attempted a replication of the experiments reported in Figures 4C–D and Supplemental Figure 1 of Sirota et al., 2011.
candidates.notes: The effect is in the expected direction (doxorubicin decreased tumor volume vs vehicle) but is not statistically significant at the Bonferroni-corrected threshold (Welch's t-test t(6.73)=2.68, uncorrected p=0.0325, Bonferroni corrected p=0.0976). Authors use hedging language ('While not statistically significant') and describe it as 'in the same direction as the original study.' The doxorubicin group had a very small sample (n=4). candidates.original_title: Discovery and preclinical validation of drug indications using compendia of public gene expression data
candidates.description: Treatment with cimetidine causes a decrease in tumor volume in A549 human lung adenocarcinoma xenografts compared with vehicle control.
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 4C–D and Supplemental Figure 1 of Sirota et al., 2011.
candidates.notes: The replication effect was in the expected direction and its reported confidence interval excluded zero, but the prespecified Bonferroni-adjusted comparison was not statistically significant; the authors describe the result as directionally consistent rather than clearly replicated.
